text: The site is now a reentry facility that helps transition previously incarcerated people into the community and is operated by GEO Group. The hearing will take place in fall 2025, with leaders from Compton's x Coalition, a group of activists trying to reclaim the site, the Public Defender's office, the Adult Probation Department and CDCR requesting to be present, according to Mahmood. -0- A recent poll found that economic concerns such as increased cost of living and inflation have become the top voting issue for young Californians. The statewide poll, conducted by Power California and Latino Decisions, examined how Californians aged 18 to 30 are navigating and responding to the first six months of the Trump administration, as well as the issues that would motivate them to turn out in the 2026 midterm elections. The poll found that inflation and housing are the most critical issues across the board to young Latino, Black, and white Californians. -0- Crews in Alameda uncovered a suspected pipe bomb in a storm drain Tuesday morning, according to police. The Alameda Police Department said the discovery happened around 10:15 a.m. near Sixth Street and Taylor Avenue, when Alameda Public Works employees halted routine maintenance after spotting the suspicious item and alerted authorities. Officers called in the Alameda County Sheriff's Office Explosive Ordnance Disposal Unit. Authorities closed nearby streets to all traffic as a precaution. -0- Oakland police are investigating the shooting deaths of two people early Tuesday morning. Police were alerted to the shooting just before 3 a.m. by a ShotSpotter gunfire detection notice in the 2400 block of Seminary Avenue. Officers found two people with gunshot wounds. Medical personnel confirmed both were dead. Police are withholding the victims' identities pending notification to next of kin. -0- A PG&E power outage was impacting most of the city of San Pablo and a large portion of Richmond Wednesday afternoon. The outage affected 3,364 customers in San Pablo and 2,749 in Richmond, according to PG&E's outage website. The company said the outage was unplanned but didn't specify a possible cause. Power was restored to most customers by 3:30 p.m. -0- Fairfield police on Tuesday arrested a man in front of a store after he was reportedly seen with a gun. At 2:12 p.m., officers responded to the 1900 block of North Texas Street following reports of a suspicious person waving a handgun around. The person, later identified as 30-year-old Israel Sloan, was with several other people in the parking lot, police said. Officers recovered the gun and allegedly found drugs on Sloan's person.
